Gate `G1` passed and is recorded in the `Gates` line as `G1 2026-10-13`, so the run stops here. The pool has 224 papers, 177 with an arXiv ID.

- `H12`: your decision is recorded in the `Halts` line. I recorded the `yes` for row 1015 myself with `tools/expand.py judge`, without dispatching an agent, because the verdict was yours rather than a new judgement. After that, `add-expand` no longer reported the conflict. Its updated `Expansion` line reads 141 in scope and 1161 rejected, and I replaced the old line with it.
- `Fetch pool data`: the 134 new papers were fetched, giving 205.
- `Fringe`: `fringe.py collect` found 120 candidates, half from each route. Two agents screened them blind, and `add-fringe` added the 19 judged in scope.
- `Fetch again`: the 19 were fetched, giving 224. The check passes, and the only notes left are a possible duplicate pair and the clustering still to come in step 3.

A few things in the report are worth your review:

- `Inconsistent screening`: the agents disagreed across ranges on several kinds of paper. These include loops with no retraining, studies of how much text is AI-generated, "knowledge collapse" in human knowledge, iterated learning, and feedback loops in predictive models. The rows on each side are listed in the report.
- `Partial unblinding`: both fringe agents fetched fuller abstracts for 14 rows, and the Asta response also carried arXiv links, which give the year away. Both say no verdict changed.
- `Possible duplicate`: the check still notes near-identical titles for `2505.21677` and `CorpusId:278959832`. It is a note, not a failure, so I left it.
- `Rule breaks`: one inline `python3 -c` read of `expand.json`, and one accidental `git diff --stat`.

The report covering all five sessions is in `runner-report.md`.
